item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.9.25, build 2724

Paint

  • Photoshop brushes: Import Photoshop brushes..., at the foot of Paint's presets, adds a Photoshop brush file's (.abr) brushes to yours as a set of their own. The menu at the top of the presets switches sets. Each brush keeps its size, roundness, angle and spacing; a brush drawn from a picture (spatter, chalk, a leaf) paints with that picture as its tip, scaled and turned with the brush. A comp keeps the tips it uses, so it renders anywhere.
  • The brush editor shows a Photoshop brush's tip under Shape; Use a round tip goes back to the round dab.
  • Grain-aware strokes, and auto grade while it's still measuring, now paint on the fast canvas too, drawn as you paint; the auto grade card still shows what it measured.

Trainer

  • A pass renders without PyTorch: each pass is saved as an ONNX file too, and a frame that isn't written yet is worked out by Kento itself once ONNX Runtime is installed (Install ONNX Runtime, under the pass). Render nodes can use a pass as it is.

Render nodes

  • A Linux render node to install: Kento's render node for Linux (x86_64) as a package of its own, unpacked and started with one command. Tried on a studio Linux box against the studio's storage: a real shot's frames match a Mac's.

Kento Alpha 0.9.24, build 2712

Trainer

  • A new node, Trainer (Other > Trainer): fix three to five frames by hand, and Trainer learns that fix and works out every other frame. Wire the plate into it and your fixed version into fixed, click Add current frame on each fixed frame, then Train. It trains on this Mac's graphics card, writes the fixed frames beside the comp so it renders anywhere, and shows the result, or the difference it makes. A pass whose training frames have changed says so.
  • Trainer needs a Python with PyTorch. Kento finds one, or you can choose it in Settings > Performance > Trainer.
  • Context frames, the temporal loss and hosted training are shown but not in Kento yet.

Paint

  • Dust, the pigment brush, warp pins on a clone, reveal or heal, and a locked auto grade now paint on RotoPaint's fast canvas, drawn as you paint. An auto grade still measuring, grain-aware strokes and cloning from Paint's own output on another frame paint as before.

Rendering and nodes

  • Bokeh and ZDefocus five times faster on a large plate: one shot's defocus went from 3.0 s to 0.55 s a frame, with the same picture.
  • ColorLookup reads its curves through a table, as Nuke does, and now matches Nuke's picture.
  • Roto curves under a scaled shape or layer are as smooth as Nuke's (the curve's pieces counted at their drawn size).

The manual

  • Every figure retaken; the Viewer's pictures show again. A section on Trainer.

Kento Alpha 0.9.23, build 2692

RotoPaint and Paint

  • Strokes paint as you draw them. What you see under the pen is the node's own render: the brush's color, softness and opacity, the eraser, a clone's source, every tool as it will look when you let go. Letting go is one undo.
  • Much faster. A new stroke costs only itself, however many are under it: on a UHD frame, RotoPaint's picture is back 0.1 s after the pen lifts with 27 strokes (was 0.4 s) and 0.16 s with 200 (was 2.6 s). Paint now paints on RotoPaint's canvas: a change takes 50 ms instead of 3 s. That covers the brush (round, oval or angled, on RGB, alpha or both, in every blend but pigment), the eraser, clone, reveal, heal, wire removal, blur, sharpen, smear, dodge and burn, and the paint-only output. Dust, pigment, warp pins, auto grade, grain-aware strokes and cloning from Paint's own output on another frame still paint as before.
  • The pointer is the brush: its outline at its size on screen, with the hardness ring inside, as in other paint programs.
  • A floating tool palette for Paint, RotoPaint and Roto: drag it anywhere or dock it at the Viewer's left edge, one or two columns, a group's other tools behind the corner of its button. Right-click it to customize: reorder tools, move them between groups, hide the ones you don't use.
  • Delete works on picked strokes and shapes, and so do every other key of the Roto and Paint tools (they never reached the tool before).
  • The right-click menu keeps what's picked, so its Cut, Copy and Delete act on it.
  • A transform box goes round several picked points, strokes or both: drag inside to move, a corner to scale, just outside a corner to turn.
  • Pressure controls in the brush menu: how much the lightest touch keeps of the size and opacity, and a light or firm response.
  • Paint's History has an × on each row to take that stroke out.
  • Paint's eraser shows under the pen even with nothing on the input.

AI roto

  • SAM 3.1 installs from Kento: Settings > Performance > AI roto > Install..., with each download's size shown first, and Resume if it stops. Isolate tracks with SAM 3.1 once it's in; SAM 2 stays as a fallback.

Viewer and Node Graph

  • Moving the pointer over a picture that's being worked out no longer holds Kento up (the pixel readout waited for the picture).
  • The keys of SplineWarp's, Perspective's and the projection plane's Viewer tools now reach them.
  • Zoomed out, a port's ring takes a click or a dropped wire where it's drawn.

Rendering

  • Render nodes render through Kento's render engine, with caches sized for a render (they rendered through Gaffer alone).
  • Kento.app carries the render node itself (Contents/Resources/kento/tools/kento_render_node.sh), so a Mac render box doesn't need to open the app.
  • Preferences > Render lists render nodes as a table, any number of them: each row shows the node's state, cores, memory and GPU, with an x to take it off the list. Add a render node... has an Add button.
  • A render node started on its own takes tasks (it refused every one), and a frame that fails says why (it showed only "Traceback").
  • A comp saved on one Mac finds its color config on the machine that opens it: by the path maps, else by the config's name among that machine's own. Kento's own configs are saved by a path that's the same on every machine. Render nodes failed every frame on a config path from the artist's Mac.
  • Renders from the Render Queue keep their caches small, as command-line renders do: a batch render of a large comp peaked at 3.2 GB instead of over 12 GB.
  • Nuke's older Shuffle and ShuffleCopy go through the render engine as one node each, and draw the right picture.
  • New comps render through Kento's render engine again (their color config's path wasn't expanded, and the render stopped).
  • Remote control's render_write sends a long range to the Render Queue and answers at once, instead of holding Kento for the whole render.

Gizmos

  • Gizmos saved as groups load: a .gizmo file holding a Group (or a NoOp with controls) instead of a Gizmo becomes that node, as in Nuke. 9 of the 23 gizmos in the studio library didn't load before.
  • Importing a gizmo no longer loses the comp's folder, which relative footage paths read from.

Remote control

  • Lists and makes Kento's own nodes (GrainMatch, Paint, Isolate and the rest), not only Nuke's.
  • Can frame the Node Graph, as F does.
  • Reads a key on a whole frame back as that whole frame.
  • Says what the Generative Grain's knobs are.
